newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania swears in reformist president.
newsitem.headline: Romania swears in reformist president.

text.p: Emil Constantinescu was sworn in as Romania's president on Friday, pledging to step up democratic reforms expected to boost his country's chances of joining NATO and the European Union.

Constantinescu took the oath before the two-house parliament dominated by his centrist followers whose victory in this month's general election threw ex-communist president Ion Iliescu's leftists out of government after seven years.

"I swear to devote all my strength and my abilities to the prosperity of the Romanian people, to defend the constitution, democracy and civic rights and freedoms," said Constantinescu, reading out the oath.
The head of the constitutional court read out a document proclaiming Constantinescu's victory over Iliescu in a run-off ballot on November 17.

"The transfer of power is the toughest test of a democracy. Romania has passed this test successfully, and has joined for good the fold of democratic states," Constantinescu, an academic with no political career under the Communists, said in his inaugural speech.
Romanian state television broadcast live the ceremony, held in a huge Bucharest palace erected by late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, toppled and shot in a 1989 upheaval.
Constantinescu, 57, elected for a four-year term, said that the Prime Minister-designate, popular Bucharest mayor Victor Ciorbea would soon announce the new coalition government.
